Those who advocate for radical upheaval often point to the American Revolution or the Declaration of Independence.

  • Right to Revolution: They cite the Enlightenment principle that when a government becomes "destructive" to the ends of life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness, it is the right and duty of the people to "throw off such Government."

  • The "Shock" to the System: Proponents argue that a violent rupture forces the entire nation to confront political realities that they believe are being ignored by a complacent public. It is seen as a way to break the "status quo."
  • Disarmament of the Opposition: By forcibly removing a regime and its supporters from power, proponents believe they can permanently neutralize what they perceive as a threat to progress, equality, or global stability.

  • Loss of Legitimacy: Violence often alienates the general public, turning potential allies away from the cause and justifying more severe state crackdowns.
